text: Antonio García Padilla, born in 1954 in Ponce, Puerto Rico, is a Puerto Rican scholar who served as president of the University of Puerto Rico from 2001 to 2009. He was born in Ponce and raised in the nearby town of Coamo, where he has five brothers, including Alejandro, who was a former senator and Governor of Puerto Rico, and Juan Carlos, who is the current mayor of Coamo, Puerto Rico. García Padilla earned a Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Magna Cum Laude, and a Juris Doctor, Magna Cum Laude, from the University of Puerto Rico. Before pursuing law, he worked in the Office of Monopolistic Affairs of the Department of Justice of Puerto Rico. He obtained an LL.M. from Yale Law School in 1981 and served as a law clerk first to the Supreme Court of Puerto Rico and then on the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit, for Judge Stephen Breyer. After his clerkship, he became an assistant professor at the University of Puerto Rico School of Law, was appointed associate dean in 1983, and dean in 1986, serving as dean until 2001 when he was elected president of the University of Puerto Rico. He assumed the presidency on 25 November 2001 and resigned on 30 September 2009. In 1999, he was elected to the Council of The American Law Institute. Currently, he chairs the Puerto Rican Academy of Jurisprudence and Legislation, is a member of the Council of the Section of Legal Education and Admissions to the Profession of the American Bar Association, which oversees law school accreditation in the United States, and is part of the Committee on Emerging Markets and Innovations of the Law School Admission Council. He has also been a member of the Council of the American Law Institute, a Commissioner of the Middle States Commission on Higher Education, and has served on numerous committees, commissions, and task forces in law and education. For seven years, he chaired the Luis Muñoz Marín Foundation of Puerto Rico. He is a member of the Iberoamerican Forum. García Padilla has been a member of the Board of Directors of Universal Insurance Co., the largest insurance company in Puerto Rico, and has served as an advisor to Universia, the association of Latin American, Spanish, and Portuguese universities supported by Banco Santander. He is also a member of the panel of commercial arbitrators of the American Arbitration Association and serves as an arbitrator in the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico. He teaches courses on Commercial Contracts, Payment Systems, Secured Transactions, and Commercial Arbitration and is a member of the Editorial Board of the Revista Jurídica de Catalunya, having published extensively in commercial law and education.
